message.content:
Interesting! In the `pj_inv` fallback path (line ~230), there's a check:
```c
if( (srcdefn->ctx->last_errno != 33 && srcdefn->ctx->last_errno != 34)
    && (srcdefn->ctx->last_errno > 0
        || srcdefn->ctx->last_errno < -44 || point_count == 1
        || transient_error[-srcdefn->ctx->last_errno] == 0 ) )
```

Here, `srcdefn->ctx->last_errno < -44` is checked BEFORE `transient_error[-last_errno]`, so if `last_errno < -44`, the short-circuit prevents the OOB access. So this path is safe.

But in `pj_datum_transform`'s `CHECK_RETURN` macro:
```c
#define CHECK_RETURN(defn) {if( defn->ctx->last_errno != 0 && (defn->ctx->last_errno > 0 || transient_error[-defn->ctx->last_errno] == 0) ) { ... }}
```
There's NO `last_errno < -44` check! So if `last_errno` is -50 to -55, `transient_error[-last_errno]` reads out of bounds.

But we need `pj_datum_transform` to be called AND `last_errno` to be set to a value < -44. Let me check when `pj_datum_transform` is called and what error codes can be set there.

Let me look at line 275 where `pj_datum_transform` is called.
